title: Merge the four surviving opencode-support proposal bullets
action: A compounding triage of docs/history/opencode-support/promote-proposals.md found 20 of its 24 area bullets already stated in the bundle and the whole onboarding column a duplicate; four bullets survive and are yours to merge, each verified live at HEAD. (1) THE STAMP TRAP, highest value: a rendered skills root that exists WITHOUT its version stamp puts installation into a blocked state that refuses and is never forceable (onboard/skills.rs:420-458); R29 in release-identity-and-version-parity.md (around :154-166) today covers only the stamp-present and legacy-fallback cases — add the missing edge case as behavior, naming what a reader would otherwise hit as an unexplainable permanent refusal. A sibling cell is adding the guarding test; describe the behavior, not the test. (2) The shipped-frame inventory now carries the third runtime's guard-file role, so a release that loses that file fails its own manifest check instead of installing nothing (release_manifest.rs:82, :399-406) — one bullet where the manifest payload and its roles are described (around :222-232), which still names only two plugin roles. (3) R31 in repo-local-guardrails.md (around :118-124) names the four pinned helper identities but not their apply lifecycle: installation also REMOVES a helper's definition file when its tier model cannot be resolved (onboard/agents.rs:231-257) — add that clause, since a helper silently disappearing is exactly what a reader needs warned. (4) In health-checks-and-proof-surfaces.md, near the deep-inventory audit (around :75-80), one line: the marker labels a source may carry are a strict superset of the runtimes whose trees are written, and an unknown label is refused rather than defaulted into some other runtime's tree (skill_trees.rs:37-49, :59). Cite the opencode-support cells (oc-4, oc-13, oc-14) as sources. Do not restate anything the bundle already says — the triage found repetition to be the proposal's dominant failure mode. Nothing else from that proposal is merged; its delivery draft and all five pattern candidates were reviewed and declined.

truths: The stamp trap is readable as behavior — a stranger knows why installation refuses and that it cannot be forced
Each of the four bullets lands under the concept that owns it, never duplicated across areas
No bullet restates something the bundle already states
Every claim cites its source cell and traces to live code

trace.outcome: Merged the four surviving opencode-support bullets (stamp trap, opencode_plugin manifest role, R31 apply lifecycle, marker-label superset) into three concept files; flushed both queued capture stubs
